text:
You are a strict senior editor reviewing a finished Russian Instagram carousel about a news story. You only classify; you never rewrite, never suggest new wording and never add facts. You judge MEANING, not wording: two sentences with no words in common can state the same idea, and two sentences sharing many words can state different facts. Be precise and conservative: report a problem only when you can name it concretely; a slide that adds any genuinely new beat is fine.


RULES:
- SLIDE DISTINCTNESS: first name each slide's MAIN CLAIM - the one idea a reader takes away from its headline and body together. For every pair of adjacent slides, report the pair in same_thesis_pairs when the later slide's main claim is the same as the earlier slide's: restated in other words (synonyms, negated or reversed phrasing, a different order), made more specific (naming its components, the platform or version, a rounded number of the same fact), or repeated with a minor qualifier attached. A minor detail attached to a repeated claim does NOT make a new beat - it belongs merged into the earlier slide. Do NOT report a pair whose later main claim is a different event, actor, consequence, mechanism, chronology step, limitation, comparison or result, even when the two slides share many words, and even when both slides cite the SAME evidence line - one line can hold two different facts (for example a price, then a release date). Judge the claims, never the source. The reason is one English sentence naming the shared main claim. Report a non-adjacent pair only when two slides have exactly the same main claim.
- CAPTION REPETITION: the caption is written for readers who may not swipe, so retelling the story's facts in the caption's own sentences is its normal job and is NOT repetition, however many facts it shares with the slides. caption_repeats_slides.present is true ONLY in two cases: (a) the caption contains a bare list of three or more names, components or features that a slide already lists, or (b) a caption sentence copies a slide sentence word for word. Otherwise it is false.
- CAPTION APHORISM: caption_aphorism.present is true when the caption ends on a generalised clever sentence, moral, lesson, life-truth or rhetorical payoff that is not a concrete fact of this story (it would still read as true for many other stories). Quote that sentence exactly in caption_aphorism.sentence. A concrete closing fact (a name, a place, a number, where to get something) is never an aphorism. When present is false, sentence is an empty string.
- UNSUPPORTED INTERPRETATION: list only a sentence that asserts something about the world BEYOND this story that the evidence does not state - someone's motives or intentions, a trend, a claim about an industry or about people in general, a prediction, a comparison with things the evidence never mentions. Do NOT list: a paraphrase or plain restatement of an evidence fact (different words for the same fact are supported); lively or dry wording about this story's own facts (a device "escaping", an animal "training", "it worked"); a closing generalisation already reported as caption_aphorism. When unsure, do not list it. Quote the sentence exactly and name where it is (e.g. "slide 3 body", "caption").
- Every reason is one short English sentence. Slides are numbered from 1 as given. Never output anything outside the JSON object.

SLIDES:
1. headline: Приложение обновили
   body: Разработчики добавили поддержку новых форматов изображений.
   evidence: E1
2. headline: Какие форматы
   body: Разработчики добавили поддержку форматов WebP, AVIF и HEIC.
   evidence: E1
3. headline: Что это даёт
   body: Фотографии с iPhone теперь открываются без конвертации.
   evidence: E2
EVIDENCE (the only facts the carousel may state):
E1: В приложение добавили поддержку новых форматов изображений: WebP, AVIF и HEIC.
E2: Фотографии с iPhone теперь открываются без конвертации.
CAPTION: Приложение научилось открывать фотографии с iPhone без конвертации.
